verdict.rationale: Fellow documents a public REST Developer API with API-key auth, cursor pagination, an OpenAPI 3.1 spec and a live Try It panel. It supports both reads (notes, recordings, transcripts, action items) and writes (agenda append, prepend, find/replace and write; action-item complete/archive; recording upload with status polling), so a user or agent can genuinely drive the product. Missing for 10: no published API changelog or deprecation policy, no Fellow-branded OpenAPI download path, API access gated to paid plans plus admin enablement with no sandbox, and no independent hands-on corroboration of end-to-end use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Developer API opens that data to you: transcripts, structured notes, and more, all available through standard REST calls.
Write a note's agenda and/or rename the note. Provide `content_fellow_markdown`, `title`, or both.
Mark an action item as complete or incomplete.
Upload a recording from a URL. Use this endpoint to bring an existing meeting recording into Fellow.
All API requests must include a valid API key in the Authorization header.
The Fellow Developer API uses cursor-based pagination for all list endpoints.
